We tested the per-model `npm` override workaround from the docs and confirmed the bug reproduces with the following stacktrace:

```
Type validation failed: Value: {"error":{"message":"list index out of range\n\nTraceback (most recent call last):\n  File \"/app/.venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/litellm/proxy/common_request_processing.py\", line 2022, in async_streaming_data_generator\n  ...\n  File \"/app/.venv/lib/python3.13/site-packages/litellm/llms/anthropic/experimental_pass_through/adapters/streaming_iterator.py\", line 819, in _should_start_new_content_block\n    if chunk.choices[0].finish_reason is not None:\n       ~~~~~~~~~~~~~^^^\nIndexError: list index out of range\n"}}
```

The root cause is visible in the trace: LiteLLM's **Anthropic pass-through streaming adapter** (`experimental_pass_through/adapters/streaming_iterator.py`) is being used to process responses from the Azure OpenAI backend (`azure/gpt-4-1-nano`). Because the per-model `npm` override is ignored, the request goes to Azure via the correct endpoint but the response is then deserialized by the Anthropic adapter, which crashes when it encounters an OpenAI-style chunk with an empty `choices` list.

This confirms the bug: the per-model `npm` field has no effect on which streaming adapter is used. The provider-level `@ai-sdk/anthropic` is applied unconditionally.

We are currently using the two-provider workaround as described in the issue.

Adding one more field report for a memory-pressure incident involving OpenCode TUI running inside Zed integrated terminal with an autonomous subagent workload.

## Environment

- OS: macOS
- Editor/terminal: Zed integrated terminal / agent panel
- OpenCode version: 1.17.7
- Provider/model: zai-coding-plan / glm-5.2
- Orchestration layer: OhMyOpenCode / Ultra Worker-style autonomous subagents
- Project shape: git worktree, large autonomous MVP build with parallel subagents

## What happened

During the run, macOS showed the memory-pressure notification asking me to quit apps. Zed was observed at around ~5 GB RAM while hosting the OpenCode TUI. The subagent workload appeared to keep spinning / not settle, so I force-closed the session.

OpenCode recorded the affected sessions as `MessageAbortedError`, not a graceful completion.

## Local evidence

Main session:

- `ses_13498fb90ffeU76kniNT952SXn`
- Title: `Autonomous debutter MVP work session`
- Agent: `Atlas - Plan Executor`
- Abort around `2026-06-15 21:18:36` local time

Subagent:

- `ses_134882271ffecsjQQ2uGCf6xtj`
- Title: `Task 2: Scaffold monorepo+tests+CI`
- Agent: `Sisyphus-Junior`
- Token total near abort: `146384`
- Final state: `MessageAbortedError` at `2026-06-15 21:18:05` local time

The subagent was actively running verification shortly before the abort:

- lint/typecheck/test/build
- Medusa migrations
- backend dev server
- `curl /health` and `/mock-status`
- idempotent DB seed verification

Zed-side evidence:

- Zed was hosting the terminal session.
- Zed logs showed a `fs_watcher lost sync` storm around `2026-06-15 20:57` local time.
- Counted roughly 500 lost-sync entries in `Zed.log` and 500 in `Zed.log.old`.

macOS unified logs:

- No explicit jetsam/SIGKILL for OpenCode or Zed found in the narrow abort window.
- OpenCode TCP connection closed around `21:19:11`.

## Possibly related

- #22198 SSE / AsyncQueue memory growth
- #16697 long-running TUI memory leaks / subagent cleanup concern
- #10913 consolidated memory leak list
- #24445 long-running TUI heap growth with OmO/plugin context
- #29730 message history/context accumulation
- #32270 memory leaks

Possibly related Zed issues:

- zed-industries/zed#53480 fs watcher lost-sync storm
- zed-industries/zed#47412 child processes not terminated
- zed-industries/zed#46474 node zombie processes
- zed-industries/zed#58742 MCP/node processes using multi-GB RAM

## Heap snapshot note / ask

I did not have a heap snapshot from the original incident. I can rerun the same workload with:

```bash
OPENCODE_AUTO_HEAP_SNAPSHOT=1 opencode
```

However, I do not want to upload a raw heap snapshot publicly without guidance because it may contain prompts, project data, env values, or other sensitive strings.

Should this stay as a comment under this memory megathread, or would maintainers prefer a separate issue? And if I reproduce with auto heap snapshots enabled, what is the preferred way to share the snapshot safely?

I had a good look at this today and I think @rekram1-node small-fixes-first path makes sense.

What's landed so far:

- #32477 fixes progress keepalive — merged
- #32478 handles the first resource notification slice (`notifications/resources/list_changed` → `mcp.resources.changed`). This is the next one I'd like to land.

Parallel to that resource work, #32480 is open for progress/status plumbing. I reworked it after feedback on the thread so mcp progress uses `session.next.tool.progress.report` instead of the partial-output path. Happy to defer broader UI if that's not the shape you want.

After #32478, the resource chain is stacked in order:

- #32936 resource subscriptions — explicit subscribe/unsubscribe, `notifications/resources/updated`, no auto-inject into context
- #32943 resource templates / completion — `resources/templates/list` and `completion/complete` at the service layer, plus error-path tests for the new methods (folded into that PR rather than a separate follow-up)

Still on the roadmap after that:

- initialize instructions — thread `InitializeResult.instructions` into model context
- elicitation — needs its own design pass (UI, permissions, accept/decline/cancel, subagents)
- sampling — policy, visibility, and budget boundaries

This split keeps the early PRs low-risk while still giving a path toward fuller MCP client support.
